# Temple Scroll Column 20 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Temple Scroll Column 20 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 20:2 — "wave offering" vs. "elevation offering" — tenufah

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a wave offering" | Traditional rendering; implies horizontal waving motion |
| LOGOS | "an elevation offering" | Modern scholarship (Milgrom) argues the gesture was vertical lifting |
| PNEUMA | "a wave offering" | Traditional and widely recognized |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "elevation offering" (LOGOS). Jacob Milgrom's research demonstrated that tenufah likely involved lifting the offering toward the deity, not horizontal waving. This is increasingly the standard in modern scholarship. However, the term remains debated; "elevation" is used with awareness that the exact gesture is uncertain.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 20:3 — "make them smoke" vs. "turn them into smoke" vs. "burn them" (recurring)

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "make them smoke upon the altar" | Literal hiqtir |
| LOGOS | "turn them into smoke on the altar" | Standard Milgrom rendering |
| PNEUMA | "burn them on the altar" | Simple "burn" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "turn into smoke" (LOGOS), consistent with Columns 18-19 rulings.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Consistent with established precedent.

---

## 20:7-8 — "wave offering/contribution" vs. "elevation offering/contribution" — tenufah/terumah pair

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "wave offering... contribution" | Traditional tenufah; terumah as "contribution" |
| LOGOS | "elevation offering... contribution" | Modern rendering for tenufah; "contribution" for terumah |
| PNEUMA | "presented... contributed" | Verbal forms instead of nouns; "the portions that were presented and set aside" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The tenufah/terumah distinction (elevation/contribution) represents two different presentation gestures and must be maintained as distinct technical terms. PNEUMA's verbal paraphrase collapses the technical vocabulary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 20:9 — "perpetual due" vs. "rightful share" — choq olam

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a perpetual due from the sons of Israel" | Literal choq olam; "due" for prescribed right |
| LOGOS | "a perpetual due for Aaron and his sons from the children of Israel" | Same; formal phrasing |
| PNEUMA | "their rightful share from the Israelites" | "Rightful share" more accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "perpetual due" (EMET/LOGOS). Choq here means an established right/claim, best rendered "due" in English legal register. "Rightful share" (PNEUMA) is acceptable but loses the "perpetual" (olam) qualifier.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 20:13 — "most holy" vs. "supremely holy" — qodesh qodashim

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "most holy" | Standard rendering of qodesh qodashim |
| LOGOS | "most holy" | Same; standard |
| PNEUMA | "supremely holy" | "Supremely" intensifies the superlative |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "most holy" (EMET/LOGOS). Qodesh qodashim is universally rendered "most holy" or "holy of holies" in English biblical translation. PNEUMA's "supremely" is non-standard.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 20:15 — "between the evenings" vs. "at twilight" vs. "in the evening" — bein ha-arbayim

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "between the evenings" | Literal bein ha-arbayim; preserves the dual form |
| LOGOS | "at twilight" | Standard modern rendering; the period between sunset and dark |
| PNEUMA | "in the evening" | Simplest English expression |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "at twilight" (LOGOS). Bein ha-arbayim is a technical chronological term debated since antiquity (Pharisees: afternoon; Samaritans/Sadducees: between sunset and dark). "At twilight" captures the ambiguity better than EMET's over-literal "between the evenings" or PNEUMA's vague "in the evening."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 20:16 — "beaten oil" vs. "pressed olive oil" — shemen katit

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "beaten oil" | Literal shemen katit |
| LOGOS | "beaten oil" | Standard; katit = crushed/beaten in a mortar |
| PNEUMA | "pressed olive oil" | "Pressed olive oil" more descriptive; specifies olive |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "beaten oil" (EMET/LOGOS). Shemen katit is a technical term for oil produced by crushing olives in a mortar rather than pressing them — a higher quality product. PNEUMA's "pressed" actually describes a different (and inferior) extraction method. The text does not need "olive" specified since shemen in cultic contexts always means olive oil.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
